status_note: Final coding of 2 November 2026, frozen and published before any count or prediction was computed. Since 0.9.2: Fischman is coded from the protective order itself (ECF 58, read free at the source); Dunn is final as not codable (the free order granting the motion describes the agreed AI provision but does not set out its words, and the protective order is PACER-only); Velez is recoded from its five provisos, now copied in full from the PDF (R13). No case is pending.
add_rules: R13 (rule self_hosted_contract_proviso). Where an order names self-hosted systems among those permitted but one of its provisos asks for a contract or contractual commitment, which setup A (no outside provider) has no one to give, setup A is coded unclear. The result is also reported with these cases coded permitted. Written while coding, after the frame was read.

replace.setup_a_quote: unless the provider of the AI Platform is contractually prohibited from
replace.setup_a_reason: The only route to use is that 'the provider of the AI Platform' is contractually bound (no training, no disclosure beyond what the service needs, deletion on request). Setup A has no outside provider, and the words do not say whether such a system is barred or outside the clause. Para. 29's conferral covers a party unsure whether a platform satisfies para. 27, so it does not open a route outside the contract test.

replace.setup_a_quote: the user has a good-faith basis to believe the platform contractually prohibits use of the information for generalized model training
replace.setup_a_reason: The order lists 'self-hosted language models' among permitted systems, but only if all five provisos hold. Setup A meets provisos 1-3 (no training for non-parties, no third-party access, safeguards), but proviso 4 asks for a good-faith basis to believe 'the platform contractually prohibits' use for model training, and setup A has no outside provider to make that promise. The words do not settle whether a self-hosted model with no such contract qualifies.
